hints.title: Write each progression before summing
hints.body: Let the first term be a and the common ratio be r. Write the first three terms, and then their squares, to identify the first term and ratio of the squared progression.
hints.recap: Taking powers of GP terms raises both the first term and the common ratio to that power.
hints.pitfall: The sum of the squares of the terms is not the square of their sum.
hints.pause: Use the two given sums to write two equations in the first term and ratio.

recall.reminder: Taking powers of GP terms raises both the first term and the common ratio to that power.

hints.title: Eliminate the first term
hints.body: Rearrange the original sum equation for the first term. Substitute it into the squared-term sum equation; factor the difference of squares in the denominator before simplifying.
hints.recap: The convergence condition permits cancellation only after excluded cases are checked.
hints.pitfall: Keep <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> in view; a denominator equal to zero would invalidate the infinite-sum formula.
hints.pause: Solve for the ratio and first term, then construct and sum the progression of cubes.

recall.reminder: The convergence condition permits cancellation only after excluded cases are checked.

solution:
1. Translate the two sums. Convergence and the nonzero sum give |r|<1. Thus a1−r=6 and a21−r2=12.

2. Eliminate the first term. Substituting a=6(1−r) gives 36(1−r)1+r=12, since neither 1−r nor 1+r is zero. Hence 3(1−r)=1+r, so r=12 and a=3.

3. Sum the cubes. They have first term a3=27 and ratio r3=18. Their sum is 271−1/8=2167. Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Recover a convergent GP from sums of its terms and squares, then sum the cubes
